questions.text: What brings you in today?
questions.rationale: Establishes the chief complaint that selects a triage pathway.

questions.text: When did this start?
questions.rationale: Onset time anchors every downstream time-sensitive consideration.

chest_pain.initial.label: Chest pain — onset & character
chest_pain.initial.description: Patient reports chest pain, discomfort, tightness, or pressure.

questions.text: Can you describe the pain — is it pressure, sharp, or burning?
questions.rationale: Character helps separate cardiac, pleuritic, and GI presentations.

questions.text: When exactly did it start, and has it been constant?
questions.rationale: Onset and pattern inform urgency and workup timing.

questions.text: Were you doing anything when it started?
questions.rationale: Exertional onset raises concern for a cardiac cause.

chest_pain.cardiac_features.label: Chest pain — cardiac features
chest_pain.cardiac_features.description: Pressure-like or exertional pain; assessing radiation and autonomic symptoms.

questions.text: Does the pain move to your arm, jaw, neck, or back?
questions.rationale: Radiation is associated with cardiac presentations.

questions.text: Any sweating, nausea, or lightheadedness with it?
questions.rationale: Autonomic features often accompany cardiac pain.

questions.text: Does anything make it better or worse — rest, exertion, position?
questions.rationale: Exertional pattern relieved by rest is a classic cardiac feature.

chest_pain.risk_factors.label: Chest pain — cardiac risk factors
chest_pain.risk_factors.description: Cardiac features present; assessing risk factor burden.

questions.text: Do you have high blood pressure, diabetes, or high cholesterol?
questions.rationale: Risk factor burden informs how strongly to consider a cardiac cause.

questions.text: Do you smoke, or have you in the past?
questions.rationale: Smoking is a major modifiable cardiac risk factor.

questions.text: Has anyone in your family had a heart attack before age 55?
questions.rationale: Early family history raises pre-test probability.

chest_pain.prior_episodes.label: Chest pain — prior episodes & history
chest_pain.prior_episodes.description: Assessing prior similar episodes and known cardiac history.

questions.text: Have you ever had pain like this before?
questions.rationale: A changed pattern from prior stable symptoms matters.

questions.text: Have you ever had a heart problem diagnosed, or a stent?
questions.rationale: Known coronary disease changes the baseline.

chest_pain.red_flags.label: Chest pain — red flags
chest_pain.red_flags.description: Screening for features that demand escalation regardless of pathway.

questions.text: Did you faint or nearly faint?
questions.rationale: Syncope with chest pain is a red-flag combination.

questions.text: Is the pain tearing or ripping, going through to your back?
questions.rationale: Tearing interscapular pain is a classic dissection descriptor.

questions.text: Is one arm weaker, or is the pain different between sides?
questions.rationale: Pulse or strength asymmetry may accompany dissection.

chest_pain.pleuritic.label: Chest pain — pleuritic features
chest_pain.pleuritic.description: Pain worse with breathing; assessing PE and pneumothorax features.

questions.text: Is the pain worse when you breathe in deeply?
questions.rationale: Pleuritic pain shifts attention toward PE, pericarditis, or pneumothorax.

questions.text: Any cough, or have you coughed up blood?
questions.rationale: Hemoptysis is associated with pulmonary embolism.

questions.text: Is one leg swollen or painful?
questions.rationale: Unilateral leg swelling suggests a DVT source.

chest_pain.pe_risk.label: Chest pain — PE risk factors
chest_pain.pe_risk.description: Pleuritic features present; assessing thromboembolic risk.

questions.text: Any long flights, car trips, surgery, or time laid up recently?
questions.rationale: Immobilization is a major provoking factor for VTE.

questions.text: Have you or your family ever had a blood clot?
questions.rationale: Prior VTE or family history raises pre-test probability.

questions.text: Are you taking hormonal contraception or hormone therapy?
questions.rationale: Estrogen-containing therapy increases clot risk.

chest_pain.gi_features.label: Chest pain — GI features
chest_pain.gi_features.description: Burning or food-related pain; assessing reflux-pattern features.

questions.text: Is it a burning feeling, and does it relate to meals?
questions.rationale: Meal-related burning suggests a reflux pattern.

questions.text: Do antacids help at all?
questions.rationale: Antacid response supports a GI pattern but does not exclude cardiac causes.

shortness_of_breath.initial.label: Shortness of breath — onset
shortness_of_breath.initial.description: Patient reports difficulty breathing or breathlessness.

questions.text: Did the breathlessness come on suddenly or gradually?
questions.rationale: Sudden onset points toward PE or pneumothorax; gradual toward cardiac or infective causes.

questions.text: Is it worse lying flat, or do you wake at night short of breath?
questions.rationale: Orthopnea and PND suggest a cardiac contribution.

questions.text: Any fever or cough with phlegm?
questions.rationale: Infective features shift toward pneumonia.

questions.text: How far can you walk now compared with a month ago?
questions.rationale: Functional change quantifies severity and trajectory.

questions.text: Any chest pain, leg swelling, or wheeze with it?
questions.rationale: Associated features steer between cardiac, embolic, and airway causes.

questions.text: Where exactly is the pain, and does it move anywhere?
questions.rationale: Location and migration pattern narrow the differential.

questions.text: Any vomiting, and can you keep fluids down?
questions.rationale: Intractable vomiting changes urgency and fluid needs.

questions.text: When did you last eat, and did that change the pain?
questions.rationale: Meal relationship distinguishes biliary and peptic patterns.

abdominal_pain.features.label: Abdominal pain — associated features
abdominal_pain.features.description: Characterizing associated GI and systemic features.

questions.text: Any fever, or blood in stool or vomit?
questions.rationale: Bleeding or fever escalates the workup.

questions.text: When was your last bowel movement, and are you passing gas?
questions.rationale: Obstipation raises concern for obstruction.
